newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Motor shuts down plants.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Motor shuts down plants.

text.p: South Korea's Hyundai Motor Co, a unit of Hyundai Group, said on Friday it was shutting down plants temporarily from 5:00 p.m. (0800 GMT) on Friday because of strikes.

"Working atmosphere and efficiency have deteriorated significantly since the strike began on December 26, and we've figured it would be for the best to close down the plants," said Lee Jun-ha, a Hyundai Motor spokesman.
Although Hyundai's union has stepped back from a full strike and decided to work several hours a day from Thursday, automobile production had not improved much, he said.

Output stood at 600 units on Thursday, compared with 4,500 to 5,000 a day normally, he said. A company statement said the strike has cost the company 43,700 cars in lost production and 400 billion won in lost sales.
The spokesman said the shutdown was temporary but did not know when the company could reopen the plants.

Shortly before the shutdown began, a Hyundai Motor worker set himself on fire during a clash between strikers from the Hyundai Group and riot police in the southeast city of Ulsan, union officials said.
Hyundai workers have been at the forefront of strikes called in protest against a new labour law which allows troubled companies to lay off workers.
Strikes have crippled much of South Korean industry since the new labour bill was passed in parliament on December 26.
